answer: Give every identity a kernel of trust that grows through verified, useful work: a newcomer first completes low-reward tasks re-checked by unrelated auditors, each success adding weight. Endorsements carry a cipher-signed trail, so a sponsor cannot quietly back dozens of clones: each endorsement is public, budgeted, and slashed if the endorsee cheats. Fake accounts mostly interact with each other, so their graph forms a tight cluster with few genuine outside links; the network detects that cluster and throttles it, so one ripple of cheating raises the cost for every sibling identity at once.
